key_insight: SANA-Video 2.0 shows that high-quality video generation can be scaled efficiently with a hybrid attention design, matching full-softmax video Diffusion Transformers while keeping linear-attention-style long-sequence efficiency. It can generate up to 720p video on a single GPU using a unified 5B/14B architecture.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high computational cost of full quadratic attention in video generation, which makes long video sequences and high-resolution outputs expensive and difficult to run on limited hardware.
method: Uses a unified hybrid video diffusion transformer architecture at 5B and 14B scales.
Combines gated linear attention for efficient O(N)-dominated token mixing with periodic gated-softmax attention anchors to preserve quality.
Adds attention residuals to improve stability and retain information across long video sequences without relying entirely on quadratic attention.
impact: This work makes high-resolution video generation more practical for researchers and practitioners by reducing memory and compute requirements. It suggests a path to scaling video models efficiently without sacrificing output quality.

paper_title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
paper_authors: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu
